questions.questionTextEn: What is the tight asymptotic solution to the recurrence T(n) = 4T(n/2) + n^2 (with T(1) = 1)?
questions.explanationEn: Here a = 4, b = 2, so n^(log_b a) = n^2. Since f(n) = n^2 = Θ(n^(log_b a)), Case 2 of the Master Theorem yields T(n) = Θ(n^2 log n).

questions.questionTextEn: Any comparison-based sorting algorithm requires at least Ω(n log n) comparisons in the worst case because:
optionsEn: A decision tree distinguishing all n! permutations must have height at least log2(n!) = Ω(n log n)
Divide and conquer always takes O(n log n)
questions.explanationEn: There are n! possible input permutations, so the binary decision tree must have at least n! leaves, giving height >= ceil(log2(n!)) = Ω(n log n).

questions.questionTextEn: In a DFS of a graph with 10 vertices, timestamps start at 1 and increment on every discovery and finish. What is the maximum finish time assigned to any vertex?
questions.explanationEn: Each of the V vertices receives one discovery timestamp and one finish timestamp, so timestamps run from 1 to `2V = 20`.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following problems exhibit the optimal substructure property?
optionsEn: Shortest simple path in a graph with positive edge weights
Longest simple path in an unweighted undirected graph
questions.explanationEn: Shortest paths (with positive weights), Matrix Chain Multiplication, and LCS all have optimal substructure. Longest simple path does NOT have optimal substructure because subpaths cannot share vertices (B is false).

questions.questionTextEn: What is the maximum number of comparisons required by Binary Search to confirm that a target key is NOT present in a sorted array of 1024 elements (counting 1 comparison per loop iteration)?
questions.explanationEn: Worst-case iterations of binary search on n elements is `floor(log2(n)) + 1 = floor(log2(1024)) + 1 = 10 + 1 = 11`.

questions.questionTextEn: Which shortest-path algorithm can detect negative-weight cycles reachable from a single source vertex in O(VE) time?
questions.explanationEn: Bellman-Ford relaxes all edges V - 1 times in O(VE) time; if any edge can still be relaxed on a V-th pass, a reachable negative-weight cycle exists.

questions.questionTextEn: What is the minimum number of leaves in the decision tree of any comparison-based sorting algorithm sorting 5 distinct elements?
questions.explanationEn: The decision tree must have at least `n! = 5! = 120` leaves to distinguish all 120 possible input permutations.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following sorting algorithms is NOT comparison-based and can sort `n` integers in range `[0, k]` in O(n + k) time?
questions.explanationEn: Counting Sort uses key values directly as array indices to count frequencies, achieving O(n + k) time without comparing pairs of keys.

questions.questionTextEn: How many valid topological orderings exist for a directed path graph `1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5`?
questions.explanationEn: A Hamiltonian directed path imposes a strict total order on all vertices, so only 1 topological ordering (`1, 2, 3, 4, 5`) exists.

questions.questionTextEn: What is the asymptotic time complexity of the recurrence T(n) = T(n - 1) + n (with T(0) = 1)?
questions.explanationEn: Expanding gives T(n) = 1 + 1 + 2 + ... + n = 1 + n(n+1)/2 = Θ(n^2).

questions.questionTextEn: What is the tight asymptotic solution to the recurrence `T(n) = 2T(√n) + log2(n)` (for n > 2)?
questions.explanationEn: Substitute `n = 2^m` (so `m = log2(n)`): `S(m) = T(2^m) = 2S(m/2) + m`. By Master Theorem, `S(m) = Θ(m log m) = Θ(log n · log log n)`.

questions.questionTextEn: Four jobs have (profit, deadline): J1(50, 2), J2(20, 1), J3(40, 2), J4(30, 1). Each job takes 1 unit of time. What is the maximum total profit achievable?
questions.explanationEn: Sort by profit descending: J1(50, d=2) -> slot 2; J3(40, d=2) -> slot 1; J4 and J2 cannot fit. Total profit = 50 + 40 = 90.

questions.topicTag: Algorithms — Binary Search on Rotated Array
questions.questionTextEn: What is the worst-case time complexity to find the minimum element in a cyclically rotated sorted array of `n` distinct integers?
questions.explanationEn: At each step, comparing `A[mid]` with `A[high]` determines which half contains the rotation pivot (minimum), halving the search space in O(log n) time.

questions.questionTextEn: In Prim's MST algorithm starting from vertex `s` in a connected graph with 8 vertices and 20 edges, how many times is an edge added to the MST?
questions.explanationEn: Prim's algorithm grows the MST one vertex and one edge at a time until all V vertices are included, adding exactly `V - 1 = 7` edges.

questions.questionTextEn: In a DFS tree of a connected undirected graph G, the root vertex `r` of the DFS tree is an articulation point (cut vertex) if and only if:
optionsEn: r has at least 2 children in the DFS tree
r has a back edge to a leaf
questions.explanationEn: Because there are no cross edges in an undirected DFS tree, two distinct subtrees of the root `r` cannot have any edges connecting them; thus removing `r` disconnects G iff `r` has >= 2 DFS children.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider a 4-vertex directed weighted graph with edges: `1->2(8)`, `1->4(2)`, `4->2(3)`, `2->3(2)`, `1->3(9)`. What is the shortest-path distance from vertex 1 to vertex 3?
questions.explanationEn: Comparing paths from 1 to 3: direct edge `1->3` costs 9; `1->2->3` costs 8 + 2 = 10; `1->4->2->3` costs 2 + 3 + 2 = 7. Shortest distance = 7.

questions.topicTag: Algorithms — Time Complexity of Nested Loops
questions.explanationEn: For each `i`, the inner loop runs `floor(n / i)` times. Summing over `i = 1..n` gives `n * (1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + ... + 1/n) = n * H_n = Θ(n log n)`.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following asymptotic relationships are TRUE?
optionsEn: n^k = O(c^n) for all constants k > 0 and c > 1
questions.explanationEn: By Stirling's formula, log(n!) = Θ(n log n) (A). `2^(n+1) = 2 * 2^n = O(2^n)` (B). Every exponential `c^n (c>1)` dominates every polynomial `n^k` (D). `2^(2n) = 4^n`, and `4^n / 2^n = 2^n -> inf`, so C is false.

questions.topicTag: Algorithms — Shortest Path in a DAG
questions.questionTextEn: What is the optimal time complexity to compute single-source shortest paths in a weighted Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) with V vertices and E edges (even if negative edge weights are present)?
questions.explanationEn: Topologically sort the DAG in O(V + E) time, then relax outgoing edges of vertices in topological order (one pass), taking O(V + E) total time even with negative weights.
